correctness.rationale: Inverse images of nonempty proper cyclic intervals under a cycle or adjacent idempotent remain cyclic intervals; only marked-left-boundary idempotents expand by exactly one. Tracking every boundary-moving inverse step bounds all reset lengths below by the minimum marked cyclic scan, and a matching backward scan constructs a word of that length. Two-mark parity formulas follow by exact visit counting. Standalone subset-BFS/word replay cross-checks 793 instances and 6083 interval cases; finite tests support, not replace, the all-n proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An upper bound or a synchronization theorem across a superclass does not entail the exact location-sensitive scanning invariant or the two-merger parity gap. The known (n-1)^2 single-merger equality is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: Reset thresholds of unitary automata on a natural cyclic graph are a central sharp-length invariant, not arbitrary finite slices. The theorem computes the optimum for every nonempty placement of merges, provides constructive shortest words, and reveals a sharp parity transition with a true geometric gap parameter in the two-site family. This determines a complete natural classification beyond the classical one-site extremal example.
